## Decision analysis · 2026-11-21T12:36Z

## 维护者速读

- 问题:在开放注册或按邮箱域名放行的自建部署里,被邀请的人自己注册后拿不到管理员给自助注册者指定的那组权限,没被邀请的注册者反而拿得到;这类部署每发一次邀请都会发生(指定的权限不是默认成员那组时才看得出差别),目前没有具名客户报告。
- 选项:A 被邀请者和普通注册者一样拿到指定权限,若管理员指定的权限组不存在或被停用,两类人注册时都被明确拒绝并提示去修配置,一个改动;B 权限组出问题时被邀请者仍能注册,但只有基础权限、事后也没人补发,要改公开约定,两到三个改动;C 只修按域名放行的部署,开放注册的照旧少发,先一个改动、以后还要再来一个;D 在 A 之外再加一道保存或启动时的权限组检查,多一个改动,而且权限组在运行中被停用时仍然拦不住。
- 推荐 A:公开约定早就写明「指定的权限组用不了时,不放任何自助注册者无权限进来」,被邀请不该成为例外,出错时当场明说也好过悄悄少发权限。
- 不定会怎样:被邀请的同事继续比不请自来的注册者少一组权限且无人察觉,已写好的修复停在开发者手里,这张带安全标签的单继续占着派发位。

## Analysis

### One-sentence problem

In a deployment that lets people sign up on their own (open to anyone, or to approved email domains), a person who was also sent an invitation ends up with less access than a stranger who was not; closing that gap makes one existing corner stricter, because when the administrator's chosen access package for self-registrants is broken, invited people who used to get in without it would now be turned away with a configuration error until it is fixed.

### Background

- The audience posture has three values. Under `open` and `email_domain` the deployment declares one permission set that every self-registrant receives (`selfRegistrationPermissionSet`); under `invite_only` the key is refused.
- Today the admission verdict asks "does this sign-up hold a pending invitation?" before it asks the posture's own rule. An invited sign-up is answered `admit, no grant` under every posture (`audience-posture.ts:685-690`), ahead of the posture switch (`:691`) whose on-allowlist arm (`:700-702`) and `open` arm (`:711-712`) answer `admit, grant`. So an invited sign-up the posture would have admitted anyway never receives the declared set. Nothing is logged for it: the grant block (`auth-manager-membership-admission.ts:345-369`) is skipped.
- PR #34969 (merged 2026-11-17T21:44Z, shipped in `@objectstack/plugin-auth` 18.6.0) made the membership binding treat an on-allowlist address as admitted by the domain rule, invitation or not. Its contract review (comment 6959636655, 2026-11-17T20:12Z, findings S1 and N1) recorded that the grant verdict and the binding now classify the same sign-up differently, and filed this card.
- The dev implemented the card's rule (one classification read by both the verdict and the binding; uncommitted) and stopped on a narrowing it measured (`os-dev-report`, comment 7062521214, 2026-11-21T12:22Z): the grant path refuses admission when the declared set cannot be resolved (`auth-manager-membership-admission.ts:357-366`). Invited on-rule sign-ups never entered that path; with the fix they do.
- The red test is not a contract pin for the behaviour that narrows. `presented-invitation.test.ts:348-372` is titled "open and email_domain match an invitation by address, as before", and its own comment (`:357-360`) says it uses a store that cannot resolve the set as a discriminator: "so `undefined` below can only be the invitation carve-out, matched by address." The file binds no security catalog (0 hits for `bindTestSecurityCatalog`), which is why its store cannot resolve the set. The `open` row depends on the old ordering as an instrument; it does not state that an invited sign-up should be admitted without the declared set.
- How reachable the narrowed corner is (measured by reading, see premises): the set name is checked for shape only when the configuration enters (`assertAudienceConfig`: non-empty, not the admin set, not an agent ceiling), and the Setup field is free text, so a mistyped or later switched-off set is reachable. In that state every uninvited sign-up is already refused `403 AUTH_CONFIG_ERROR` with an error-level log line naming the set. The corner is therefore "a deployment whose self-registration is already wholly refused, plus an invited person whose address the posture admits".

### Governing text

- Spec docblock, `packages/spec/src/system/auth-config.zod.ts:475-486` (found by `git grep -n "nobody is admitted ungranted" origin/main -- packages/spec/src/system/auth-config.zod.ts` → `:483`): "The permission set a SELF-REGISTRANT receives … Refused for `invite_only` (inert there: invited/provisioned users receive grants from their invitation placement or operator assignment, not from this key). The enforcement side refuses admission when the named set cannot be resolved (dangling declaration ⇒ nobody is admitted ungranted)". The describe text at `:488`: "Name of the permission set granted to each self-registrant."
- ADR-0093, amendment note under D1 and D7 ledger row (found by `git grep -n "admitted by the domain rule" origin/main -- docs/adr` → `0093-…:179`, `:486`): "Under `email_domain`, an address on the allowlist is admitted by the domain rule and binds as before." This rules the classification for binding; it says nothing about the grant.
- Released changelog, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/CHANGELOG.md:8792` (found by `git grep -n "a declaration that cannot be resolved refuses admission" origin/main -- packages/plugins/plugin-auth/CHANGELOG.md`): a self-registration posture "grants each self-registrant the DECLARED permission set (`sys_user_permission_set`); a declaration that cannot be resolved refuses admission (`403 AUTH_CONFIG_ERROR`) rather than admitting ungranted."
- Epic #11723 (the audience-posture decision card; its RULED block adopts option A, whose invariants include 「自助注册者获得的权限集必须显式声明」) and its execution card #11739, invariant 3 (read with `gh api repos/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/11723` and `…/11739`).
- ADR-0078 §1 (`docs/adr/0078-no-silently-inert-metadata.md:52`): "*Parsed, unmarked, silently inert* is prohibited".
- Implementation-level text that points the other way, lower in rank than the spec: module doc `audience-posture.ts:59-66` ("a self-serve creation holding a PENDING, unexpired `sys_invitation` row is admitted under every posture") and the code comment at `:686-688` ("An explicit invitation is a stronger operator act than any posture"). PR #35200 (merged 2026-11-19T22:28Z) already placed one rule ahead of that carve-out (an unverified social creation is refused, and "a pending invitation addressed to it does not admit it either", module doc `:89-92`), so the sentence is no longer absolute on main.
- None found: no ADR decides whether an invitation overrides the unresolvable-set refusal. Search: `git grep -n -i -E "self-registr|selfRegistrationPermissionSet" origin/main -- docs/adr` → 0 lines; the same terms plus "audience posture" in `AGENTS.md` → 0 lines.

### Protocol statement

The protocol (the spec docblock above, restated by the released changelog) declares two things: a self-registrant under `open` or `email_domain` receives the declared set, and a declared set that cannot be resolved means nobody is admitted without it. The code on main does neither for one population, an invited sign-up the posture's own rule admits: it is admitted without the set always, resolvable or not.

- A, C and D do not change the protocol. A brings the code to it for both postures; C for one.
- B changes the protocol: it adds an exception to "nobody is admitted ungranted" (an invited sign-up is). Under the dispatch rule that spec outranks implementation and a protocol change takes its own card, B is not a legitimate arm of this bug card as written; it would need a spec docblock edit under `packages/spec/src/**`, which the claim on this card forbids without a stop-and-report.
- Because the governing text points one way, what remains for the maintainer is not a choice between two readings of the contract. It is the confirmation of a BREAKING narrowing on a permission boundary, which sits on the human floor regardless.

### Premises (each with a re-check and its reading at origin/main 615d9954)

1. The invitation is read before the posture rule and answers no grant. `git grep -n -E "if \(hasPendingInvitation\) \{|switch \(audience\.posture\) \{" origin/main -- packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/audience-posture.ts` → `:685`, `:691`. Holds.
2. An uninvited sign-up with an unresolvable declared set is already refused, fail-closed. Code: `git grep -n "const resolvable = await this.selfRegistrationSetResolvable" origin/main -- packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-membership-admission.ts` → `:357`, inside `if (verdict.grantPermissionSet)` at `:345`, returning `AUTH_CONFIG_ERROR` at `:366`. Pins: `git grep -n -E "DANGLING declared permission set|activation ledger switches OFF refuses admission" origin/main -- packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/audience-posture.test.ts` → `:893` (not in the catalog: 403, code `AUTH_CONFIG_ERROR`, message names the set, no user row) and `:908` (switched off in the activation ledger: same). Holds by reading; not executed here (see confidence gaps).
3. The invitation-only path grants nothing from the declared set. `invite_only` with an invitation and `email_domain` off the allowlist both end at `audience-posture.ts:689` (`grantPermissionSet: false`); unit pins `audience-posture.test.ts:301-309` and `:331-340`. What such a person receives is the membership and role written when they accept the invitation. A leaves this as it is; the dev's verdict table says so too.
4. The red test is a discriminator, not a contract pin. `sed -n 348,372p packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/presented-invitation.test.ts`; `git grep -c "bindTestSecurityCatalog" origin/main -- packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/presented-invitation.test.ts` → no output (0). Holds.
5. The set is not validated for existence before sign-up time. `git grep -n -E "typeof set !== 'string' \|\| set.length === 0|set === 'admin_full_access'" origin/main -- packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/audience-posture.ts` → `:338`, `:345` (shape and forbidden names only; the function is synchronous and takes no engine, `:277-281`); `git grep -n -B2 "key: 'audience_self_registration_permission_set'" origin/main -- packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/auth.manifest.ts` → `type: 'text'` at `:132`. The only existence check is `selfRegistrationSetResolvable` (`auth-manager.ts:3416`), called from the admission path alone. So the corner is reachable by a typo, by switching the set off later, or by a composition with no security catalog.
6. A full store outage already refuses the invited sign-up today. `git grep -n "Unanswerable ⇒ no carve-out" origin/main -- packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts` → `:3137` (the invitation probe's `catch` answers false, so the posture applies and the grant path refuses). The "store unavailable" part of the narrowing is therefore limited to a partial failure where the invitation read succeeds and the catalog or ledger read does not.
7. Who can be in this state at all. `git grep -n -E "posture: *'(open|email_domain)'|selfRegistrationPermissionSet" origin/main -- examples | wc -l` → 0; the same search over the hotcrm checkout → 0; a cloud-managed environment is refused every posture but `invite_only` (`audience-posture.ts:299-304`). The exposed population is self-hosted deployments that opened sign-up and also send invitations. No customer is named on the card (triage comments 6960533723 and 7014051683).
8. Nothing moved under the dev's base. `git log --oneline 8145424b53..origin/main -- packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/audience-posture.ts packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-membership-admission.ts packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/presented-invitation.test.ts packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/invitation-acceptance-verified-address.test.ts packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/audience-posture.test.ts packages/spec/src/system/auth-config.zod.ts content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx` → empty. The dev's measurements at 8145424b53 carry to 615d9954 for these files.
9. A boot or save-time existence check cannot remove the runtime branch. The set's standing is read live from the security catalog and the activation ledger at each sign-up (`catalog-set-in-effect.ts:72-83`), and the ledger can switch a set off after boot (pin `audience-posture.test.ts:908`). A check at entry reduces how often the branch is reached; it does not make it unreachable, so the question on this card still needs its answer.

### The concrete question

When the card's rule lands (an invited sign-up the posture admits receives the declared set, like an uninvited one), what happens to that sign-up if the declared set cannot be resolved: is it refused like every other self-registrant (the narrowing), or does the invitation still let it in without the set?

### Options

| Option | What it does | Customer-visible consequence | Effort |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| A. One rule, fail-closed | The posture's own rule is read first, by the grant and the binding alike. An invited sign-up it admits is a self-registrant: it receives the declared set, and takes the same refusal when the set cannot be resolved. An invitation still admits by itself where the posture does not (`invite_only`; `email_domain` off the allowlist), with no grant, as today. | Invited colleagues get the same access as anyone who signs up. On a deployment whose declared set is broken, an invited person the posture admits is now refused with the configuration error that uninvited people already get, until an administrator corrects the set or creates the account directly. ### Business meaning per option

- A: "An invitation adds a seat and a role; it never takes away what the front door gives everyone." If the front door's access package is broken, the door is shut for everyone it would have served, with a sign on it saying what to fix.
- B: "If the access package is broken, invited guests are waved in anyway with a visitor badge, and nobody comes back later to give them the real one." Convenient on the day, and the source of accounts that look normal and stay short of access.
- C: "Fix the side entrance, leave the main entrance as it is." A second trip is certain.
- D: "Add a second inspector at the factory because the one at the door is strict." It catches typos sooner; it does not replace the one at the door.

### Four axes

- Long-term soundness. The product needs one answer to "who is a self-registrant", read by every consequence of sign-up (the access granted, the organization joined, the verification asked). A is that: it removes the case where an invitation changes what a person the posture admits receives, and it aligns the grant with the binding that PR #34969 already settled. B keeps a second answer for one state (a broken set plus an invitation) and writes an exception into a published promise. C leaves the two answers standing under `open`. D adds a check and leaves the runtime answer still to be given. (Mechanism: the invitation branch ahead of the posture switch in `decideAudienceAdmission`; `isAdmittedByInvitationAlone`.)
- Business pull, measured. No customer is named on the card; triage rated it p2. No example app and no hotcrm source declares these two postures (0 hits), and cloud-managed environments cannot. So the fix serves self-hosted deployments that open sign-up and also invite people, which is a normal combination but an unmeasured population. For the narrowed corner specifically there is no evidence of any deployment relying on invited people getting in while the declared set is broken, and in that state the deployment's self-registration is already refused for everyone else. Zero pull for keeping that path.
- AI error. Take a deployment an AI configured with a set name that does not exist. Under A every sign-up the posture admits, invited or not, sees a loud refusal: a 403 whose message names the set and the fix, and an error-level log line; no account is created. Under B uninvited people see that refusal and invited people are silently under-granted: created, signed in, baseline access only, nothing retries. On main today invited people are silently under-granted even when the configuration is correct. No option over-grants: the declared set is what any sign-up the posture admits already receives.
- Do not sprawl. A adds no key, no error code, no setting and no state; it deletes a branch. B adds a fallback state, a spec exception and possibly an ADR row, each a standing obligation. C costs two rounds for one rule. D is a new check: new gates default to no, no maintainer statement names one for this, and it does not remove the corner.

### Recommendation

**A.** The published contract already says that a declared set which cannot be resolved admits no self-registrant without it, and the classification settled for binding makes an invited sign-up the posture admits a self-registrant. A is the code catching up with both, as one BREAKING patch; the corner it narrows is a deployment whose self-registration is already refused, and the refusal is loud and names its remedy.

- Not B: it contradicts the spec sentence it would have to amend, and it manufactures accounts short of their declared access that nothing repairs.
- Not C: half of one rule, still BREAKING, and the `open` half returns as a second card.
- Not D: it cannot remove the runtime branch (a set can be switched off after boot), and it is a new check with no measured pull. If the maintainer wants typos caught at save, that is a separate card and not a condition of A.

A's first-axis reading is not close to the others, so the effort difference (1 PR against 2 to 3 for B) is not what decides it.

Confidence gaps, stated and not used to move the recommendation:

1. No test was executed for this analysis: the read-only checkout has no installed dependencies. Premises 2 to 4 are readings of code and test text. The single red test is the dev's measured run at 8145424b53, and premise 8 shows the files unchanged since.
2. The dev's uncommitted patch was not available. Its shape is taken from the report. The dev measured the narrowing under `open` only; the `email_domain` on-allowlist case "follows from the same code, not separately measured".
3. How many self-hosted deployments run `open` or `email_domain` with invitations is unknown; the repository carries no such telemetry.
4. That the under-grant is invisible when the declared set is the member baseline is read from a docblock (`platform-baseline-sets.ts:10`), not executed.
5. Whether `Metadata-protocol: none` is the right kind, or `semantic` because the key now reaches invited sign-ups, is for the contract-tier review; #34969 and #35200 both shipped `none`.
6. Under A an invitation can expire while the set is broken (the invitation mail's window is stated as 48 hours by default in the plugin-auth changelog; not checked against the installed vendor), so the administrator may have to re-invite after fixing the set.

### End state

In two years a person's sign-up is classified once and every consequence reads that one answer: someone the deployment's own sign-up rule admits always receives the declared access, an invitation adds an organization and a role on top of it and never replaces it, and a declared access package that cannot be found stops sign-up loudly until an administrator repairs it. That is how the mainstream platforms model it: Salesforce Experience Cloud self-registration creates every self-registered user with the configured default profile and none without one, and Okta, Auth0 and Entra self-service sign-up with domain allowlists treat an invitation as added organization roles on top of the sign-up default.
